body.statement:
The fixed exponent-two class is contained in the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi observational class:
\[
 \mathcal M_\star\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}.
\]
body.proof_tex: Take \(P_X\in\mathcal M_\star\).  By \(\mathrm{def:lower\text{-}class}\), \(P_X\in\mathcal M\), and \(\mathrm{def:fourier\text{-}model}\) supplies \(X=AH+G_\Gamma\) with \(U=AH\), \(U\perp G_\Gamma\), \(1\le k\le p\), mutually independent nonconstant source coordinates, \(\operatorname{Var}(H_j)=1\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=k\), lexicographically sorted columns, and no nondegenerate Gaussian convolution divisor for any \(H_j\). Because \(A\) has full column rank, it has a deterministic linear left inverse \(L=(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), so \(H=LU\) is a measurable function of \(U\); hence \(U\perp G_\Gamma\) implies \(H\perp G_\Gamma\). Independence and the unit variances give \(\operatorname{Cov}(H)=I_k\).  A nonconstant Gaussian variable has a nondegenerate Gaussian convolution divisor (split its positive variance into two positive summands), so Gaussian indecomposability also implies that every \(H_j\) is non-Gaussian.  Every defining condition of \(\mathrm{def:sr\text{-}published\text{-}class}\) follows, proving \(P_X\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\).
